name: Fortress of Suomenlinna
description: Suomenlinna is a sea fortress spread across a cluster of rocky islands guarding Helsinki's harbour, a short ferry ride from the city centre. Sweden began building it in 1748 as a defence against Russia, adapting French star-fort designs to the uneven terrain. Once nicknamed the "Gibraltar of the North," it now draws locals and visitors to its bastions, walls and island picnic spots.
